title: Cellular small object factorizations in locally presentable categories
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with Hom sets in a fixed universe $\mathcal U$ and all $\mathcal U$-small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose $\mathcal C$ is locally presentable: for some infinite regular cardinal $\lambda\in\mathcal U$, a $\mathcal U$-small set of objects $\mathcal P$ generates every object under $\lambda$-filtered colimits and $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ preserves those colimits for every $P\in\mathcal P$. Here $\lambda$-filtered means that every diagram with fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms admits a cocone, and regular means that a union of fewer than $\lambda$ sets of size less than $\lambda$ has size less than $\lambda$. Let $I$ be a $\mathcal U$-small set of morphisms. For every $f:X\to Y$ there is a factorization $X\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{p}Y$ with $pj=f$, such that $p$ has the right lifting property against $I$ and $j$ is a transfinite composition of pushouts of small coproducts of maps of $I$. Explicitly, there are a $\mathcal U$-small ordinal $\theta$ and objects $Z_\alpha$ for $\alpha\leq\theta$, with $Z_0=X$, $Z_\theta=Z$, and $j$ their composite, continuous at every limit ordinal, such that $Z_\alpha\to Z_{\alpha+1}$ is a pushout of $\coprod_{t\in T_\alpha}i_t$ for a $\mathcal U$-small set $T_\alpha$ and maps $i_t\in I$. Continuity means $Z_\beta=\varinjlim_{\alpha<\beta}Z_\alpha$ at every nonzero limit $\beta\leq\theta$. Right lifting means that for every $i:A\to B$ in $I$ and square $pa=bi$ with $a:A\to Z$, $b:B\to Y$, there is $h:B\to Z$ with $hi=a$ and $ph=b$.

proof.text: Write the small set of generators as $I=\{i:A_i\to B_i\}$. For every $i\in I$, apply [lem-coef-object-presentability-rank] to $A_i$ in the given locally presentable category. Choose an infinite regular cardinal $\tau_i\in\mathcal U$ such that $\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,-)$ preserves every $\mathcal U$-small $\tau_i$-filtered colimit. These choices concern only the domains; there is no presentability assumption on $X$, $Y$, or the codomains $B_i$.

For $i\in I$, let $T_i$ be the set of ordinals below the initial ordinal of cardinality $\tau_i$. The tagged disjoint union $T=\coprod_{i\in I}T_i$ is $\mathcal U$-small. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to obtain an infinite regular $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ with $|T|<\kappa$. Each inclusion $t\mapsto(i,t)$ proves $\tau_i=|T_i|\leq |T|<\kappa$. If $I$ is empty the same lemma applies to the empty disjoint union, and still gives an infinite regular $\kappa$. Below, also write $\kappa$ for its initial ordinal.

source.place: Agent proof, a uniform bound for the domains; Mathlib SetTheory/Cardinal/HasCardinalLT.lean:199-206.

proof.text: The ordinal category of $\alpha<\kappa$ is $\tau_i$-filtered for every $i$. A diagram with fewer than $\tau_i$ morphisms has fewer than $\tau_i$ objects, since every object has an identity. Its object images are fewer than $\kappa$ ordinals below $\kappa$. Their union has cardinality less than $\kappa$ by regularity, and hence is an ordinal $\beta<\kappa$ bounding all images. The unique arrows to $\beta$ give a cocone. For the empty diagram use $0$. Thus the preservation in step 1 applies to every diagram indexed by $\kappa$. This ordinal is also a nonempty directed poset, so its colimits of sets are filtered colimits. Since $\kappa$ is an infinite initial ordinal it is a nonzero limit ordinal: for any $\alpha<\kappa$ the ordinal $\alpha+1$ still has cardinality less than $\kappa$ and is below $\kappa$.

source.place: Agent proof, regular-union argument using the definitions of regularity, filteredness and initial ordinal.

proof.text: Specify the successor operation at any map $q:V\to Y$. Let $Q(q)$ be the set of triples $(i,a,b)$ with $i\in I$, $a:A_i\to V$, $b:B_i\to Y$, and $qa=bi$. It is $\mathcal U$-small, being a subset of the small disjoint union of the sets $\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,V)\times\operatorname{Hom}(B_i,Y)$. Form $A(q)=\coprod_{(i,a,b)\in Q(q)}A_i$ and $B(q)=\coprod_{(i,a,b)\in Q(q)}B_i$. The summand maps define $a_q:A(q)\to V$, $i_q:A(q)\to B(q)$ and $b_q:B(q)\to Y$ with $qa_q=b_qi_q$. Choose their pushout $s(q)=V\amalg_{A(q)}B(q)$, with maps $c_q:V\to s(q)$ and $e_q:B(q)\to s(q)$. These coproducts and this pushout exist as colimits of small discrete and span diagrams. Their universal properties give $q^+:s(q)\to Y$ with $q^+c_q=q$ and $q^+e_q=b_q$. For a summand $t=(i,a,b)$ put $d_t=e_q\iota_t:B_i\to s(q)$. The pushout equation gives $d_ti=c_qa$ and $q^+d_t=b$. This proves the required filler at the next stage directly, by the defining colimit equations.

source.place: Agent construction by coproduct and pushout universal properties; compare Mathlib SmallObject/Construction.lean:FunctorObjIndex, functorObj, functorObj_comm, and ιFunctorObj_extension.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-transfinite-recursion] on the small well-order $\{\beta:\beta\leq\kappa\}$ to construct objects $Z_\beta$, maps $p_\beta:Z_\beta\to Y$ and transition maps $u_{\alpha\beta}:Z_\alpha\to Z_\beta$ for $\alpha\leq\beta$, with inductive invariant $u_{\alpha\alpha}=1$, $u_{\beta\gamma}u_{\alpha\beta}=u_{\alpha\gamma}$ and $p_\beta u_{\alpha\beta}=p_\alpha$. Here is the entire recursion rule. At zero set $Z_0=X$ and $p_0=f$. At $\beta=\alpha+1$ use step 4 on $p_\alpha$: set $Z_\beta=s(p_\alpha)$, $p_\beta=p_\alpha^+$, $u_{\alpha\beta}=c_{p_\alpha}$ and $u_{\delta\beta}=c_{p_\alpha}u_{\delta\alpha}$ for $\delta<\alpha$. Set the new identity transition to $1$. The composition equations and the equation over $Y$ follow immediately from the previous invariant and $p_\alpha^+c_{p_\alpha}=p_\alpha$. At a nonzero limit $\beta$, take the colimit of the already coherent diagram $(Z_\alpha)_{\alpha<\beta}$ and let $u_{\alpha\beta}$ be its cocone maps. The compatible maps $p_\alpha$ give $p_\beta$ by the colimit universal property. The cocone equations give all new composition equations, and the definition of $p_\beta$ gives its equations over $Y$. Thus the invariant holds at zero, successors and limits. To apply the quoted recursion to a rule defined on every family, take its value collection to contain all such stage records and a dummy symbol; on a prefix that is not a coherent family of the required records let the rule return the dummy symbol. The three checks just given show by well-order induction that the actual recursively produced family never takes that value. This specifies a total recursion rule, rather than assuming that arbitrary earlier records already form a diagram. Every colimit used at a limit is small, since $\beta\leq\kappa\in\mathcal U$.

source.place: Agent categorical recursion, with successor and limit rules and coherence invariant written out; the recursion leaf is WellFoundedLT.fix/fix_eq, Mathlib Order/RelClasses.lean:304-313. proof.text: Put $Z=Z_\kappa$, $j=u_{0\kappa}$ and $p=p_\kappa$. The invariant gives $pj=p_0=f$. At every nonzero limit $\beta\leq\kappa$, the chosen $Z_\beta$ is the colimit of the preceding stages by step 5. For each $\alpha<\kappa$, its transition to $Z_{\alpha+1}$ is exactly the pushout map $c_{p_\alpha}$ of step 4, a pushout of the coproduct of the maps $i$ indexed by $Q(p_\alpha)$. Consequently this is the specified cellular presentation of $j$, with $\theta=\kappa$ and $T_\alpha=Q(p_\alpha)$; no inference from a left lifting property or from a retract of a cellular map is made.

source.place: Agent proof, unpack the constructed chain and its invariant; the ordinal and all attaching sets have already been bounded.

proof.text: To prove right lifting, fix $i:A_i\to B_i$ in $I$ and maps $a:A_i\to Z$, $b:B_i\to Y$ with $pa=bi$. Since $\kappa$ is a nonzero limit ordinal, step 5 identifies $Z$ with the colimit of $(Z_\alpha)_{\alpha<\kappa}$. By steps 1 and 3, applying $\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,-)$ to this cocone gives a colimit cocone of sets whose vertex is $\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,Z)$ and whose legs send $v$ to $u_{\alpha\kappa}v$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] to its element $a$. Obtain $\alpha<\kappa$ and $a_\alpha:A_i\to Z_\alpha$ with $u_{\alpha\kappa}a_\alpha=a$. The invariant implies $p_\alpha a_\alpha=p u_{\alpha\kappa}a_\alpha=pa=bi$. Hence $(i,a_\alpha,b)$ is one of the actual triples attached at stage $\alpha$, without any need to descend a further equality or to assume $B_i$ presentable.

source.place: Stacks Tag 04AX, categories-section-directed-colimits, filtered colimits of sets as a quotient of their disjoint union; apply clause (1) to the Hom-colimit preserved by presentability.

proof.text: Let $d:B_i\to Z_{\alpha+1}$ be the summand map of step 4 for that triple. It satisfies $di=c_{p_\alpha}a_\alpha$ and $p_{\alpha+1}d=b$. Define $h=u_{\alpha+1,\kappa}d$. Since $\alpha+1<\kappa$, this transition exists, and the invariant gives $hi=u_{\alpha\kappa}a_\alpha=a$ and $ph=p_{\alpha+1}d=b$. Thus $p$ has the required right lifting property. If $I$ is empty, the lifting condition is vacuous, each attaching coproduct is initial and its pushout map is an isomorphism; the same construction and all limit arguments remain valid. Empty attaching sets at individual stages are handled by the same initial-object pushout.
